messages:
Maya: heads-up — after last night's runtime tweak we got a sustained p99 tail for tenant `acme-pay`. Small requests (~30 tokens) are fine p50/p95 but p99 jumped ~420ms. Rolling back helped briefly then returned. Anyone seen this pattern? :eyes:

Dan: saw the alert, digging. Quick suspicion: compact coalescer change in 2026-06-10 deploy that lowered max_wait_ms for micro-requests. Could cause more tiny batches stuck waiting for a fill threshold.

Leo: can you paste the current continuous-batcher config for that pool?

Maya: here you go — it's what the last deploy pushed (from infra canary):
```
continuous_batcher:
  strategy: compact-coalesce
  max_batch_size: 32
  min_batch_fill: 0.3
  hold_timeout_ms: 12
  max_wait_ms: 40
  grace_window_ms: 6
  prefix_cache_enabled: true
```

Sara: interesting — min_batch_fill 0.3 + hold_timeout 12ms means low-volume tiny prompts might not hit fill and wait the full 40ms. That stack can cause long tails if many requests arrive just after batch dispatch.

Dan: agree. The quick mitigation we used last time was to lower max_wait_ms -> 8ms for the smallest tenant pools and bump grace_window to 10ms. That reduces the variance. We should test.

Maya: repro steps I used: 1) send steady 60 RPS of 20-token requests to tenant's route 2) interleave bursts of 1-3 requests every 200ms 3) measure p99 on the route. I can share a tiny load script if helpful.

Maya: log snippet during spike: `rpc_recv->schedule_batch delay=43ms, batch_size=2, held=28ms, dispatch_latency=210ms`

Leo: that dispatch_latency looks like queuing in the runtime (serializing lots of small KV-cache merges). Could also be CPU worker saturation on that host. Any host-level CPU p95 high?

Maya: CPU flat at ~60% but python worker threads show occasional lock contention traces when small-batch merge runs.

Sara: two-pronged plan: (1) short-term: canary change on one pool -> max_wait_ms: 8, grace_window_ms: 10, min_batch_fill: 0.2 (2) medium: add early-dispatch heuristic: if held_count > 1 and average_payload_tokens < 40, dispatch early. (3) long-term: telemetry to emit per-request hold_ms + merge_time to pinpoint runtime hotspots.

Dan: I'll cut the canary now on pool `us-west-2-compact-3`. Rolling config via rollout-id r-2026-06-11-compact-fix. Canary for 10 minutes, then extend if p99 improves.

support-bot: deploy started r-2026-06-11-compact-fix -> pools: us-west-2-compact-3 (canary) by Dan. :rocket:

Maya: after canary apply (5 min warmup) p99 dropped from 420ms -> 95ms on that pool. p95 stable. Early signs good.

Leo: nice. Can we add a quick guard in routing to fallback to slightly higher batch_size variants if caller latency sensitivity flag isn't set? Means we prefer throughput routes for background jobs.

Sara: yes — routing policy change limited to dedicated/tenant routes only. We'll avoid host-wide routing churn.

Dan: can we also add a short-lived metric: continuous_batcher.hold_time_histogram and continuous_batcher.merge_ms to cloudwatch today? I'll wire alerts if p99 of hold_time > 30ms.

Maya: adding load-script and repro steps to the incident ticket. If the canary stays green for 30m I'll roll to remaining pools.

Support-bot: deploy succeeded r-2026-06-11-compact-fix -> canary stable after 15m.

Maya: rolling to all compact pools now. Will keep monitoring p99. Thanks team. :heart:
